source.text: Ἐπιστραφεὶς ὁ Πέτρος βλέπει τὸν μαθητὴν ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀκολουθοῦντα, ὃς καὶ ἀνέπεσεν ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν· Κύριε, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παραδιδούς σε;

records.literal_gloss: Having turned, the Peter sees the disciple whom loved the Jesus following, who also reclined at the supper on the chest of him and said, Lord, who is the [one] handing over you?

en.L: Having turned around, Peter sees the disciple whom Jesus loved following, the one who also had leaned back on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chest at the supper and said, "Lord, who is it that is handing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} over?"
en.B: Peter turned around and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them, the same disciple who at the supper had leaned back against Jesus's chest and said, "Lord, who is it that is going to betray {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.R: Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved. That disciple was following them too. At the last supper, this was the disciple who had leaned back against Jesus's chest and asked, "Lord, who is it that will betray {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

es.L: Volviéndose, Pedro ve al discípulo a quien Jesús amaba, que seguía, el que también en la cena se había recostado sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pecho y había dicho: «Señor, ¿quién es el que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} entrega?».
es.B: Pedro se volvió y vio que los seguía el discípulo a quien Jesús amaba, aquel que durante la cena se había inclinado hacia atrás sobre el pecho de Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} había preguntado: «Señor, ¿quién es el que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} va a traicionar?».
es.R: Pedro se volvió y vio al discípulo a quien Jesús amaba. Ese discípulo también los seguía. Era el que, en la última cena, se había inclinado hacia atrás sobre el pecho de Jesús para preguntarle: «Señor, ¿quién {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} va a traicionar?».

fr.L: S’étant retourné, Pierre voit le disciple que Jésus aimait, qui suivait, celui qui aussi, pendant le souper, s’était penché sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} poitrine et avait dit : « Seigneur, qui est celui qui {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} livre ? »
fr.B: Pierre se retourna et vit le disciple que Jésus aimait qui les suivait, celui-là même qui, pendant le souper, s’était penché contre la poitrine de Jésus et avait dit : « Seigneur, qui est celui qui va {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} trahir ? »
fr.R: Pierre s’est retourné et il a vu le disciple que Jésus aimait. Ce disciple les suivait, lui aussi. Pendant le dernier repas, c’était lui qui s’était penché contre la poitrine de Jésus et qui avait demandé : « Seigneur, qui va {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} trahir ? »

sw.L: Petro, akigeuka, anamwona yule mwanafunzi ambaye Yesu alimpenda akifuata, yule ambaye pia wakati wa chakula cha jioni aliegemea kifuani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}} na kusema, "Bwana, ni nani anayekutoa?"
sw.B: Petro aligeuka, akamwona yule mwanafunzi ambaye Yesu alimpenda akiwafuata, yule yule ambaye wakati wa chakula cha jioni alikuwa ameegemea kifuani pa Yesu na kuuliza, "Bwana, ni nani atakayekusaliti?"
sw.R: Petro aligeuka, akamwona yule mwanafunzi ambaye Yesu alimpenda. Mwanafunzi huyo naye alikuwa akiwafuata. Wakati wa chakula cha jioni cha mwisho, yeye ndiye aliyekuwa ameegemea kifuani pa Yesu na kumwuliza, "Bwana, ni nani atakayekusaliti?"

vi.L: Phi-e-rơ quay lại, thấy môn đồ mà Đức Giê-xu yêu đang đi theo, là người cũng đã ngả mình vào ngực {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong bữa ăn tối và nói: "Lạy Chúa, ai là kẻ nộp Chúa?"
vi.B: Phi-e-rơ quay lại và thấy môn đồ mà Đức Giê-xu yêu đang đi theo họ. Đó là môn đồ đã ngả người tựa vào ngực Đức Giê-xu trong bữa ăn tối và hỏi: "Lạy Chúa, ai là kẻ sẽ phản bội Chúa?"
vi.R: Phi-e-rơ quay lại và thấy môn đồ mà Đức Giê-xu yêu. Môn đồ ấy cũng đang đi theo họ. Trong bữa ăn tối cuối cùng, chính môn đồ này đã ngả người tựa vào ngực Đức Giê-xu và hỏi: "Thưa Chúa, ai là người sẽ phản bội Chúa?"

ko.L: 베드로가 돌아서서, 예수께서 사랑하시는 제자가 따라오는 것을 본다. 그는 만찬 때에 그분의 가슴에 기대어 "주님, 주님을 넘겨주는 사람이 누구입니까?" 하고 말했던 사람이다.
ko.B: 베드로가 돌아서서 보니, 예수께서 사랑하시는 제자가 따라오고 있었다. 그는 만찬 때 예수의 가슴 쪽으로 몸을 기대고 "주님, 주님을 배반할 사람이 누구입니까?" 하고 여쭈었던 제자였다.
ko.R: 베드로가 뒤돌아보니, 예수께서 사랑하시는 제자가 그들을 따라오고 있었다. 이 제자는 마지막 만찬 때 예수의 가슴에 기대어 "주님, 주님을 배반할 사람이 누구입니까?" 하고 여쭈었던 바로 그 제자였다.

decisions.choice: the disciple whom Jesus loved: the unnamed disciple of 13:23, 19:26, 20:2 and 21:7
decisions.reason: The Gospel never names him. This sentence ties him to the night of the last supper, so that readers know which disciple is meant before verse 24 says that he is the one who testifies to these things and wrote them.

decisions.choice: who also had reclined ... and said: a reminder of 13:23-25, pointing back to that night
alternatives: a new event at a different meal
decisions.reason: "The supper" is the meal of 13:2, where this disciple lay next to Jesus and leaned back against his chest to ask who the betrayer was (13:25). The same verb and the same word for "chest" are used here. John recalls the scene to show who this disciple is: the one closest to Jesus on the night he was handed over.

decisions.choice: following: walking behind Jesus and Peter, with an echo of following as a disciple
alternatives: following only in the plain sense
decisions.reason: Jesus has just said to Peter, "Follow me" (verse 19), and the two seem to be walking together. The other disciple comes after them. John uses the same verb for following Jesus as a disciple (1:37-43; 8:12; 12:26), and verse 22 picks it up again, so the plain sense likely carries this second one as well.

decisions.choice: handing you over: betraying you, said of Judas
alternatives: handing over in a neutral sense
decisions.reason: As in 6:64, 6:71, 12:4 and 13:21, the verb means to hand someone over, and used of Judas it means betrayal. The present tense in the question at the supper spoke of what was about to happen.

decisions.choice: sees, says (L); saw, asked, said (B, R)
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("he sees", "he says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage (verses 20, 21 and 22).

decisions.choice: leaned back; Lord, who is it ...; handing you over (L); betray (B, R); following them (B, R); the last supper (R)
alternatives: Lord, who is the one betraying you?
decisions.reason: The recalled words keep the English of 13:25 ("leaning back", "Lord, who is it?"). As in 13:21, Literal keeps the plain sense of "hand over", and Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was (meaning decision m4). Balanced and Readable supply "them" for the ones he followed, Jesus and Peter (m3), and Readable names the meal so that young readers know which supper is meant (m2).

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal ("ve", "dice"); pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps the present tense in which John tells some past events; Balanced and Readable use the pretérito, as Spanish tells a story. This applies to every such verb in the passage (verses 20, 21 and 22).

decisions.choice: el discípulo a quien Jesús amaba; recostado (L); inclinado hacia atrás (B, R); te entrega (L); te va a traicionar (B, R); los seguía (B, R); la última cena (R)
decisions.reason: The beloved disciple keeps the book-wide wording. The recalled scene keeps each level's Spanish of 13:25 and 13:21 (meaning decisions m2, m4): Literal the plain sense of "entregar", Balanced and Readable what Judas's handing over was. Balanced and Readable supply "los" for Jesus and Peter (m3), and Readable names the meal. "Su", "te" and "le" for Jesus take the deity_pronoun setting (1:1).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("Pierre voit", "Pierre dit", "Jésus lui dit"); passé composé (R); speech in the present and passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (21:20-25). The passé simple ("se retourna", "se répandit") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (verses 20, 21 and 22), as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("Pierre s'est retourné"). The plus-que-parfait ("s'était penché", "avait dit") at every level marks what happened earlier, at the supper (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} livre (L); va {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} trahir (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb, to hand over, and Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was (meaning decision m4), as the English does. The French present "livre" can speak of what is about to happen, as the Greek present does; Balanced and Readable make that explicit with "va".

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal ("anamwona", "anamwambia"); -li- then -ka- at Balanced; plain past at Readable
decisions.reason: John tells parts of this scene in the present tense ("he sees", "he says", verses 20, 21 and 22). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced uses -li- for the first verb of a sequence and -ka- for those that follow, as written Swahili narrative does, and Readable tells it in the plain past. This holds for the whole passage. Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb, so the reader setting for pronouns for Christ falls only on free pronouns and possessives, such as "mwake" here.

decisions.choice: anayekutoa (L); atakayekusaliti (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 13:21 in this translation, Literal keeps the plain sense of "hand over" ("kutoa"), and Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was, betrayal (meaning decision m4). "Bwana, ni nani" and "kifuani pa Yesu" repeat the Swahili of 13:25, so the reader knows the scene recalled.

decisions.choice: "nộp" (L); "phản bội" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "nộp" is the literal "hand over"; Balanced and Readable say plainly what the handing over was.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} for Jesus in the narrative; "Chúa" as the disciples' "you"
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the whole book; "Chúa" is a noun of address and takes no span.

decisions.choice: historic present "본다", "말한다", "말씀하신다" (L); past tense (B, R), through 21:20-25
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present in narrative; Balanced and Readable use the past. One decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: "예수께서 사랑하시는 제자" at every level; "주님을" for "you" in the disciple's question
decisions.reason: The fixed designation of the beloved disciple through the book (see 21:7); disciples address Jesus as "주님" and never "당신" (style guide, section 4). No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through 21:20-25: Korean has no capital letters.

source.text: τοῦτον οὖν ἰδὼν ὁ Πέτρος λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Κύριε, οὗτος δὲ τί;

records.literal_gloss: This one therefore having seen, the Peter says to the Jesus, Lord, this one and what?

en.L: So, having seen this one, Peter says to Jesus, "Lord, and what about this one?"
en.B: When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, "Lord, and what about him?"
en.R: When Peter saw him, he asked Jesus, "Lord, what will happen to him?"

es.L: Al ver, pues, a este, Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice a Jesús: «Señor, ¿y este qué?».
es.B: Al verlo, Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo a Jesús: «Señor, ¿y él qué?».
es.R: Cuando Pedro lo vio, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó a Jesús: «Señor, ¿qué le va a pasar a él?».

fr.L: Ayant donc vu celui-ci, Pierre dit à Jésus : « Seigneur, et celui-ci, quoi ? »
fr.B: En le voyant, Pierre dit à Jésus : « Seigneur, et lui ? »
fr.R: Quand Pierre l’a vu, il a demandé à Jésus : « Seigneur, et lui, qu’est-ce qui va lui arriver ? »

sw.L: Basi Petro, akimwona huyu, anamwambia Yesu, "Bwana, na huyu je?"
sw.B: Petro alipomwona, akamwambia Yesu, "Bwana, na huyu je?"
sw.R: Petro alipomwona, akamwuliza Yesu, "Bwana, itakuwaje kwa huyu?"

vi.L: Vậy khi thấy người này, Phi-e-rơ nói với Đức Giê-xu: "Lạy Chúa, còn người này thì sao?"
vi.B: Thấy môn đồ ấy, Phi-e-rơ hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Lạy Chúa, còn người này thì sao?"
vi.R: Thấy môn đồ ấy, Phi-e-rơ hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Thưa Chúa, rồi người này sẽ ra sao?"

ko.L: 그러므로 베드로가 그를 보고 예수께 말한다. "주님, 이 사람은 어떻게 [됩니까]?"
ko.B: 베드로가 그를 보고 예수께 여쭈었다. "주님, 이 사람은 어떻게 됩니까?"
ko.R: 베드로가 그 제자를 보고 예수께 여쭈었다. "주님, 이 사람은 앞으로 어떻게 됩니까?"

decisions.choice: this one and what?: what will happen to him?
decisions.reason: The Greek is a short question with no verb. Jesus has just told Peter how he will die (verses 18-19), so the question most naturally asks about the other disciple's future: what will become of him? John does not say why Peter asked, whether from concern for his friend or from wanting to compare their lots.

decisions.choice: and: setting this disciple beside Peter himself
decisions.reason: The small word sets the other disciple against what has just been said about Peter: "and he?", "what about him, then?" Jesus's answer (verse 22) keeps the same contrast: "you, follow me".

decisions.choice: Lord: the address of a disciple to his master
decisions.reason: As at the supper (13:25, 36-37) and earlier in this chapter (21:15-17), Peter speaks to Jesus as "Lord".

decisions.choice: what about him (B); what will happen to him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the short, open question; Readable says in full what it asks (meaning decision m1). Both use the past tense (see verse 20, rendering decision r-en-1).

decisions.choice: ¿qué le va a pasar a él? (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the short question with no verb; Readable says in full what it asks (meaning decision m1). "Él" here is the other disciple and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: Seigneur, et lui ?
alternatives: Seigneur, et celui-ci, que lui arrivera-t-il ?
decisions.reason: French has the same short question without a verb as the Greek (meaning decisions m1 and m2): "Et lui ?" sets the other disciple beside Peter and leaves open what Peter wants to know. Readable says in full what it asks, as the English Readable does. "Lui" refers to the other disciple, so it takes no setting.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐὰν αὐτὸν θέλω μένειν ἕως ἔρχομαι, τί πρὸς σέ;

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the Jesus, If him I want to remain until I come, what to you?

en.L: Jesus says to him, "If I want him to remain until I come, what [is that] to you?
en.B: Jesus said to him, "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Suppose I want him to stay alive until I come back. What does that matter to you?

es.L: Le dice Jesús: «Si quiero que él permanezca hasta que yo venga, ¿qué [es eso] para ti?
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «Si quiero que él permanezca hasta que yo venga, ¿qué te importa a ti?
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Supongamos que quiero que él siga vivo hasta que yo vuelva. ¿Qué tiene que ver eso contigo?

fr.L: Jésus lui dit : « Si je veux qu’il demeure jusqu’à ce que je vienne, qu’[est-ce que cela] te [fait] ?
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Si je veux qu’il demeure jusqu’à ce que je vienne, en quoi cela te regarde-t-il ?
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Imaginons que je veuille qu’il reste en vie jusqu’à ce que je revienne. Qu’est-ce que cela peut te faire ?

sw.L: Yesu anamwambia, "Nikitaka yeye akae mpaka ninapokuja, [hilo] ni nini kwako?
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Kama ningetaka adumu hadi nitakapokuja, hilo linakuhusu nini?
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Tuseme nataka aendelee kuishi hadi nitakaporudi. Hilo linakuhusu nini?

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn người ấy ở lại cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến, thì [việc đó] liên quan gì đến con?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn người ấy ở lại cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến, thì việc đó có liên quan gì đến con?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Giả sử {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn người ấy còn sống cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trở lại. Việc đó thì liên quan gì đến con?

ko.L: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하신다. "내가 올 때까지 그가 머무르기를 내가 원한다 하더라도, 그것이 너에게 무슨 [상관이냐]?
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 올 때까지 그가 머무르기를 내가 바란다고 해도, 그것이 너와 무슨 상관이냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "내가 다시 올 때까지 그가 살아 있기를 내가 바란다고 하자. 그것이 너와 무슨 상관이 있느냐?

decisions.choice: remain: stay alive, go on living
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to live on, as in 12:34 ("the Christ remains forever") and 1 Corinthians 15:6, where most of the witnesses "remain" until now, that is, are still alive. That is the sense here: verse 23 shows that people took it to mean the disciple would not die. It is the same verb John uses for remaining in Jesus (15:4-10), but nothing in the context points to that sense here.

decisions.choice: if I want: a supposition, not a promise
alternatives: a promise that he will live until Jesus comes
decisions.reason: The form puts a case: "suppose that I want". Jesus does not say that he does want it, as verse 23 is careful to point out. What happens to the other disciple is Jesus's own choice, as Peter's death is (verses 18-19).

decisions.choice: until I come: Jesus's coming again at the end
alternatives: his coming to the disciples after the resurrection
his coming at a person's death
decisions.reason: Jesus has promised to come again and take his disciples to himself (14:3). The followers of verse 23 understood the words of his return, and the correction there does not dispute that sense; it only denies that Jesus made a promise. The present tense "I come" refers to the future, as often with this verb.

decisions.choice: what is that to you?: that is not your concern
decisions.reason: The phrase, literally "what to you?", tells Peter that the other disciple's future is not his business. Jesus turns him back from comparing to his own call.

decisions.choice: remain (L, B); stay alive (R); come back (R); what does that matter to you (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "remain", John's word throughout (see the book's terms), so that verses 22 and 23 read as the same saying that was misunderstood; the context makes the sense plain (meaning decision m1). Readable says "stay alive" and "come back" (m3), turns the "if" into "suppose" (m2) and puts the idiom into plain words (m4).

decisions.choice: permanezca (L, B); siga vivo (R); venga (L, B); vuelva (R); ¿qué [es eso] para ti? (L); ¿qué te importa a ti? (B); ¿Qué tiene que ver eso contigo? (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "permanecer", John's word throughout, so that verses 22 and 23 read as the same saying that was misunderstood; the context makes the sense plain (meaning decision m1). Readable says "siga vivo" and "vuelva" (m3), turns the "if" into "supongamos" (m2) and puts the idiom into plain words (m4). The quotation runs on into the next sentence and closes after "sígueme".

decisions.choice: demeure (L, B); reste en vie (R); jusqu'à ce que je vienne (L, B); revienne (R); qu'[est-ce que cela] te [fait] (L); en quoi cela te regarde-t-il (B); Qu'est-ce que cela peut te faire (R)
decisions.reason: French "demeurer" can mean to go on living as well as to stay, so Literal and Balanced keep the book's word and verses 22 and 23 read as the same saying that was misunderstood (meaning decision m1). Readable says "rester en vie" and "revenir" (m3), turns the "if" into "Imaginons que" (m2), and puts the idiom into plain words (m4). Literal brackets the words French needs for the bare Greek "what to you?".

decisions.choice: the quotation stays open to the end of the next sentence
alternatives: close the quotation here, as the English does
decisions.reason: Both sentences are Jesus's answer to Peter, so French closes the quotation marks at the end of verse 22, as other passages do when a speech runs across records.

decisions.choice: akae (L); adumu (B); aendelee kuishi (R)
decisions.reason: "Kukaa" is the word for "remain" throughout John, and Literal keeps it so that verses 22 and 23 read as the one saying. Here it means to go on living (meaning decision m1), which Balanced says with "kudumu", as at 12:34, and Readable plainly with "aendelee kuishi". Balanced puts the supposition in the conditional "ningetaka" (if I should want), since Jesus does not say that he does want it (m2); Readable says "Tuseme" (suppose), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ở lại" (L, B); "còn sống" (R)
decisions.reason: "ở lại" is the book-wide word for menein; Readable says the sense the meaning decision gives. Jesus says "Ta" and calls Peter "con", as in 21:15-19.

decisions.choice: "머무르다" (L, B); "살아 있다" (R)
decisions.reason: "머무르다" is the book's word for menō, so Literal and Balanced keep the thread; the meaning decision says it means to stay alive here, which Readable says plainly.

decisions.choice: Jesus's quotation runs on to the end of verse 22: no closing mark here, closed after "너는 나를 따라라"
alternatives: closing the quotation after "상관이냐?" as the English stores it
decisions.reason: "You follow me" in the next sentence is still Jesus speaking, so the Korean keeps both sentences inside one quotation.

decisions.choice: you: stressed, in contrast with the other disciple
decisions.reason: The Greek does not need the pronoun with a command, so its presence, at the head of the sentence, puts weight on it: whatever happens to him, you are to follow me.

decisions.choice: follow me: go on following Jesus as his disciple, to the end
decisions.reason: The command repeats verse 19, and the present tense means to keep on following. After the words about Peter's death (verses 18-19) it also recalls 13:36, "you will follow me later": Peter is to follow Jesus even in dying for him. These are the last words of Jesus in the Gospel.

decisions.choice: As for you (B); But you must (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare "you"; Balanced and Readable show the stress and the contrast with the other disciple in natural words (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Tú sígueme (L); En cuanto a ti, sígueme (B); ¡Tú sígueme! (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek pronoun is stressed, setting Peter against the other disciple (meaning decision m1); Spanish shows it by writing "tú" before the command, and Balanced with "en cuanto a ti". "Tú" here is Peter, and "me" is joined to the verb, so neither takes a setting (1:1).

decisions.choice: Toi, suis-moi (L)
decisions.reason: French shows the stressed "you" (meaning decision m1) with "toi" at the head of the sentence, as the Greek has it, so Literal needs no added words; Balanced and Readable bring out the contrast with the other disciple, as the English does.

source.text: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν οὗτος ὁ λόγος εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι ὁ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος οὐκ ἀποθνῄσκει.

records.literal_gloss: Went out therefore this the word to the brothers that the disciple that not dies.

en.L: So this word went out to the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that that disciple does not die.
en.B: So the saying spread among the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} that this disciple would not die.
en.R: So word spread among the believers that this disciple would not die.

es.L: Salió, pues, esta palabra hacia los {{gender:hermanos y hermanas|hermanos}}: que aquel discípulo no muere.
es.B: Por eso corrió entre los {{gender:hermanos y hermanas|hermanos}} la voz de que ese discípulo no iba a morir.
es.R: Por eso, entre los creyentes se empezó a decir que ese discípulo no iba a morir.

fr.L: Cette parole sortit donc vers les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, que ce disciple-là ne meurt pas.
fr.B: Le bruit se répandit donc parmi les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} que ce disciple ne mourrait pas.
fr.R: Alors, chez les croyants, on a commencé à dire que ce disciple ne mourrait pas.

sw.L: Basi neno hili likatoka kwenda kwa ndugu, kwamba mwanafunzi yule hafi.
sw.B: Basi habari hii ilienea kati ya ndugu kwamba mwanafunzi huyo hatakufa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo habari ilienea kati ya waumini kwamba mwanafunzi huyo hatakufa.

vi.L: Vậy lời này đồn ra giữa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} rằng môn đồ ấy không chết.
vi.B: Vì thế, lời ấy lan truyền trong vòng {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} rằng môn đồ này sẽ không chết.
vi.R: Vì vậy, các tín hữu đồn với nhau rằng môn đồ này sẽ không chết.

ko.L: 그러므로 그 제자는 죽지 않는다는 이 말이 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들에게 퍼져 나갔다.
ko.B: 그래서 그 제자는 죽지 않을 것이라는 말이 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들 사이에 퍼졌다.
ko.R: 그래서 믿는 사람들 사이에 그 제자는 죽지 않을 것이라는 소문이 퍼졌다.

decisions.choice: the brothers: the community of believers, men and women
decisions.reason: On the day of the resurrection Jesus called his disciples "my brothers" (20:17). Here the word is used, as often in Acts and the letters (Acts 1:15-16; 9:30), for believers in general, the community that told and handed on the story. The masculine plural covers a mixed group.

decisions.choice: this word went out: the saying of verse 22 spread, understood in a certain way
decisions.reason: "This word" is Jesus's saying about the disciple remaining until he comes, or the conclusion people drew from it. It "went out", that is, it was passed on from person to person.

decisions.choice: does not die: the present tense, meaning that he would not die
decisions.reason: Greek keeps the tense of the words as they were first said. The believers took "remain until I come" to mean that this disciple would still be alive when Jesus returned.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} (L, B); the believers (R)
decisions.reason: The brothers are the whole community of believers, men and women (meaning decision m1), so the inclusive form is the default and "brothers" the alternative, as at 20:17. Readable says "the believers", which is already inclusive and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: spread; would not die
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the natural verb for news passing from person to person (meaning decision m2), and the tense that reported speech takes in this language (m3).

decisions.choice: {{gender:hermanos y hermanas|hermanos}} (L, B); los creyentes (R)
decisions.reason: The brothers are the whole community of believers, men and women (meaning decision m1), so the inclusive form is the default and "hermanos" the alternative, as in English. Readable says "los creyentes", which is already inclusive and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: corrió ... la voz (B); se empezó a decir (R); no iba a morir (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for news passing from person to person (meaning decision m2), and the tense that reported speech takes in Spanish (m3).

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} (L, B); les croyants (R)
decisions.reason: The brothers are the whole community of believers, men and women (meaning decision m1), so the inclusive form is the default and the traditional "frères" the alternative, unlike Jesus's brothers at 2:12. Readable says "les croyants", already inclusive. Balanced says "le bruit", the French for a report passed from person to person (m2), and puts the reported words in the conditional (m3).

decisions.choice: ndugu (L, B), with no gender span; waumini (R)
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already covers men and women, the whole community of believers (meaning decision m1), so the Swahili needs no gender setting where the English has one. Readable says "waumini" (believers), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} (L, B); "các tín hữu" (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's only gender span, for adelphoi meaning the believers.

decisions.choice: {{gender:형제자매|형제}}들 (L, B); "믿는 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the community of believers, men and women, is meant; this is the one gender span the style guide allows (section 7). Readable says "believers" as the English does. The clause "that that disciple does not die" is placed before "이 말", as Korean requires.

source.text: οὐκ εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι οὐκ ἀποθνῄσκει ἀλλ’· Ἐὰν αὐτὸν θέλω μένειν ἕως ἔρχομαι, τί πρὸς σέ;

records.literal_gloss: Not said however to him the Jesus that not he dies, but, If him I want to remain until I come, what to you?

en.L: But Jesus did not say to him that he does not die, but, "If I want him to remain until I come, what [is that] to you?"
en.B: But Jesus had not told Peter that the disciple would not die; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said, "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?"
en.R: But Jesus did not say that this disciple would not die. He only said, "Suppose I want him to stay alive until I come back. What does that matter to you?"

es.L: Pero Jesús no le dijo que no muere, sino: «Si quiero que él permanezca hasta que yo venga, ¿qué [es eso] para ti?».
es.B: Pero Jesús no le había dicho a Pedro que ese discípulo no iba a morir; le había dicho: «Si quiero que él permanezca hasta que yo venga, ¿qué te importa a ti?».
es.R: Pero Jesús no dijo que ese discípulo no iba a morir. Solo dijo: «Supongamos que quiero que él siga vivo hasta que yo vuelva. ¿Qué tiene que ver eso contigo?».

fr.L: Or Jésus ne lui dit pas qu’il ne meurt pas, mais : « Si je veux qu’il demeure jusqu’à ce que je vienne, qu’[est-ce que cela] te [fait] ? »
fr.B: Pourtant Jésus n’avait pas dit à Pierre que ce disciple ne mourrait pas ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit : « Si je veux qu’il demeure jusqu’à ce que je vienne, en quoi cela te regarde-t-il ? »
fr.R: Mais Jésus n’avait pas dit que ce disciple ne mourrait pas. Il avait seulement dit : « Imaginons que je veuille qu’il reste en vie jusqu’à ce que je revienne. Qu’est-ce que cela peut te faire ? »

sw.L: Lakini Yesu hakumwambia kwamba hafi, bali, "Nikitaka yeye akae mpaka ninapokuja, [hilo] ni nini kwako?"
sw.B: Lakini Yesu hakuwa amemwambia Petro kwamba mwanafunzi huyo hatakufa; alikuwa amesema, "Kama ningetaka adumu hadi nitakapokuja, hilo linakuhusu nini?"
sw.R: Lakini Yesu hakusema kwamba mwanafunzi huyo hatakufa. Alisema tu, "Tuseme nataka aendelee kuishi hadi nitakaporudi. Hilo linakuhusu nini?"

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu đã không nói với ông rằng người ấy không chết, mà [nói]: "Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn người ấy ở lại cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến, thì [việc đó] liên quan gì đến con?"
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không hề nói với Phi-e-rơ rằng môn đồ ấy sẽ không chết; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chỉ nói: "Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn người ấy ở lại cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến, thì việc đó có liên quan gì đến con?"
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không nói rằng môn đồ này sẽ không chết. Ngài chỉ nói: "Giả sử {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} muốn người ấy còn sống cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trở lại. Việc đó thì liên quan gì đến con?"

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서는 그에게 그가 죽지 않는다고 말씀하지 않으셨고, 다만 "내가 올 때까지 그가 머무르기를 내가 원한다 하더라도, 그것이 너에게 무슨 [상관이냐]?" [하고 말씀하셨다].
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서는 베드로에게 그 제자가 죽지 않을 것이라고 말씀하신 것이 아니라, "내가 올 때까지 그가 머무르기를 내가 바란다고 해도, 그것이 너와 무슨 상관이냐?" 하고 말씀하셨을 뿐이다.
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서는 그 제자가 죽지 않을 것이라고 말씀하지 않으셨다. 다만 이렇게 말씀하셨을 뿐이다. "내가 다시 올 때까지 그가 살아 있기를 내가 바란다고 하자. 그것이 너와 무슨 상관이 있느냐?"

decisions.choice: what is that to you? is part of the quotation (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the quotation ends at "until I come"
decisions.reason: A few witnesses, among them the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and some early translations, leave out the last words of the quotation. Most manuscripts repeat Jesus's words of verse 22 in full, and the SBLGNT prints them. The meaning is not affected. A footnote gives the shorter reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: not ... but: a correction quoting Jesus's exact words
decisions.reason: The writer sets the rumor against what Jesus actually said. By repeating the saying word for word, he shows that it was a supposition ("if I want"), not a promise, and leaves the disciple's future in Jesus's hands.

decisions.choice: the correction may suggest that the disciple had died, or was old, when this was written
alternatives: the correction was made while the disciple was still in good health, only to set the record straight
decisions.reason: If believers expected this disciple to live until Jesus returned, his death, or his great age, would have raised the question of whether Jesus had been wrong. The careful correction would meet that question. The text does not say so, and it is possible that the correction was made for another reason. Verse 24 speaks of the disciple's testimony in the present tense.

decisions.choice: Peter, the disciple (B); this disciple, only (R)
alternatives: to him that he does not die (L)
decisions.reason: In the Greek "him" is Peter and "he" is the other disciple; Balanced and Readable name each so that the pronouns are not confused. Readable gives "but" as "only", since the point is that Jesus said no more than this (meaning decision m2). The saying keeps the wording it has in verse 22 at each level.

decisions.choice: a Pedro, ese discípulo (B); ese discípulo, Solo (R)
alternatives: no le dijo que no muere (Literal)
decisions.reason: In the Greek "him" is Peter and "he" is the other disciple; Balanced and Readable name each so that the reader does not confuse them, and Readable gives "sino" as "solo", since Jesus said no more than this (meaning decision m2). The saying keeps the wording it has in verse 22 at each level.

source.text: Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ μαθητὴς ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ τούτων καὶ ὁ γράψας ταῦτα, καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς αὐτοῦ ἡ μαρτυρία ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: This is the disciple the [one] testifying concerning these things and the [one] having written these things, and we know that true of him the testimony is.

en.L: This is the disciple who testifies concerning these things and who wrote these things, and we know that his testimony is true.
en.B: This is the disciple who is testifying about these things and who has written them, and we know his testimony is true.
en.R: This disciple is the one who tells about these things, and he is the one who wrote them down. We know that what he says can be trusted.

es.L: Este es el discípulo que da testimonio acerca de estas cosas y el que escribió estas cosas, y sabemos que verdadero es su testimonio.
es.B: Este es el discípulo que da testimonio sobre estos hechos y que los ha puesto por escrito. Y sabemos que su testimonio es verdadero.
es.R: Este discípulo es el que cuenta estas cosas, y él es quien las escribió. Sabemos que lo que dice es digno de confianza.

fr.L: Celui-ci est le disciple qui rend témoignage au sujet de ces choses et qui a écrit ces choses, et nous savons que son témoignage est vrai.
fr.B: C’est ce disciple qui rend témoignage de ces choses et qui les a écrites ; et nous savons que son témoignage est vrai.
fr.R: C’est ce disciple qui raconte ces choses, et c’est lui qui les a écrites. Nous savons qu’on peut se fier à ce qu’il dit.

sw.L: Huyu ni yule mwanafunzi anayeshuhudia kuhusu mambo haya na aliyeandika mambo haya, na tunafahamu kwamba ushuhuda wake ni wa kweli.
sw.B: Mwanafunzi huyu ndiye anayeshuhudia kuhusu mambo haya, na ndiye aliyeyaandika. Tunajua kwamba ushuhuda wake ni wa kweli.
sw.R: Mwanafunzi huyu ndiye anayewaambia watu habari za mambo haya, na ndiye aliyeyaandika. Tunajua kwamba anayoyasema yanaaminika.

vi.L: Đây là môn đồ làm chứng về những việc này và đã viết những điều này, và chúng tôi biết rằng lời chứng của ông là thật.
vi.B: Chính môn đồ này đang làm chứng về những việc ấy và đã viết lại những điều này; chúng tôi biết lời chứng của ông là thật.
vi.R: Môn đồ này là người kể lại những việc ấy, và cũng là người đã viết ra. Chúng tôi biết những gì ông nói là đáng tin.

ko.L: 이 사람이 이 일들에 대하여 증언하고 이것들을 기록한 제자이다. 그리고 우리는 그의 증언이 참되다는 것을 안다.
ko.B: 이 일들을 증언하고 또 이것들을 기록한 사람이 바로 이 제자이다. 우리는 그의 증언이 참되다는 것을 안다.
ko.R: 이 일들을 증언하는 사람이 바로 이 제자이고, 이것을 글로 적은 사람도 그이다. 우리는 그의 증언을 믿을 수 있다는 것을 안다.

decisions.choice: this is the disciple: the disciple whom Jesus loved (verse 20)
decisions.reason: "This" points back to the disciple of verses 20-23. The Gospel ends by naming him as its witness, yet still does not give his name. He was at the supper (13:23), at the cross (19:26-27, 35) and at the empty tomb (20:2-8).

decisions.choice: wrote these things: wrote them himself, or had them written
alternatives: wrote down some of these things, later included in the book
decisions.reason: The verb normally means that he wrote. It can also be used of one who has something written, as Pilate "wrote" the title on the cross (19:19-22) though others will have done the lettering. The sentence may mean that the disciple wrote the Gospel with his own hand, or that he stands behind it as its source and author. "These things" may be the whole Gospel or the account just told; the next verse looks back over the whole book.

decisions.choice: we know: a group who vouch for the disciple's witness
alternatives: the writer speaking of himself as "we" (compare 1:14; 3:11)
decisions.reason: The sentence speaks of the disciple as "he" and then says "we know". The most natural reading is that others, perhaps the community that knew him and issued the Gospel, add their own word that his testimony can be relied on, as two witnesses make a testimony valid (8:17). The disciple himself could be speaking with others in the plural, as in 1:14 ("we have seen his glory"), or including his readers. John does not say who "we" are.

decisions.choice: testifying ... his testimony is true: an eyewitness whose account can be relied on
decisions.reason: "Testify" and "testimony" run through the Gospel (1:7, 34; 5:31-39; 8:13-18; 15:27). The words echo 19:35, where the one who saw testifies and "his testimony is true". The present "testifies" may mean that he is still bearing witness, in person or through the book.

decisions.choice: testifies, testimony (L, B); tells about, what he says (R); wrote (L); has written (B); wrote them down (R)
alternatives: caused these things to be written
decisions.reason: "Testify" and "testimony" are the words used elsewhere in John, and "his testimony is true" matches 19:35. Readable uses everyday words for the same ideas, as in 19:35. Every level keeps "wrote", which leaves the question in meaning decision m2 open, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: da testimonio, testimonio ... verdadero (L, B); cuenta, lo que dice es digno de confianza (R); escribió (L, R); ha puesto por escrito (B)
decisions.reason: "Dar testimonio" and "testimonio" are the words used elsewhere in John (15:26-27), and "su testimonio es verdadero" keeps the echo of 19:35 (meaning decision m4). Literal keeps the Greek order "verdadero es su testimonio". Readable uses everyday words for the same ideas. Every level keeps a plain verb of writing, which leaves the question in m2 open.

decisions.choice: rend témoignage, son témoignage est vrai (L, B); raconte, on peut se fier à ce qu'il dit (R); a écrit (every level)
decisions.reason: "Rendre témoignage" and "le témoignage" are the book-wide words, and "son témoignage est vrai" should match 19:35 (meaning decision m4). Readable uses everyday words for the same ideas, as the English Readable does. Every level says "a écrit", which leaves open, as the Greek does, whether he wrote with his own hand or had it written (m2).

decisions.choice: anayeshuhudia, ushuhuda (L, B); anayewaambia watu habari za, anayoyasema yanaaminika (R)
decisions.reason: "Kushuhudia" and "ushuhuda" are the words for testifying and testimony throughout John (meaning decision m4). Readable uses everyday words for the same ideas, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "chúng tôi" for "we know"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say whether "we" includes the reader: the meaning decision reads it as a group vouching for the disciple to the readers, so the exclusive "chúng tôi".

decisions.choice: "증언하다", "증언" at every level, Readable included
alternatives: "전해 주다", "그가 하는 말" (R), as the English Readable
decisions.reason: "증언" is the book-wide term for testimony (style guide, section 6) and is common Korean; keeping it shows this disciple as a witness, which the meaning decision stresses.

source.text: ἔστιν δὲ καὶ ἄλλα πολλὰ ἃ ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἅτινα ἐὰν γράφηται καθ’ ἕν, οὐδ’ αὐτὸν οἶμαι τὸν κόσμον χωρήσειν τὰ γραφόμενα βιβλία.

records.literal_gloss: There are now also other many things which did the Jesus, which if they should be written one by one, not even itself I suppose the world to contain the being written books.

en.L: And there are also many other things which Jesus did, which, if they were written one by one, I suppose not even the world itself would contain the books being written.
en.B: Jesus did many other things as well. If each one were written down, I suppose that even the world itself could not hold all the books that would be written.
en.R: Jesus also did many other things. If every one of them were written down, I do not think the whole world would have room for all the books that would be written!

es.L: Y hay además muchas otras cosas que hizo Jesús; si se escribieran una a una, supongo que ni el mundo mismo podría contener los libros que se escribieran.
es.B: Jesús hizo además muchas otras cosas. Si se pusiera por escrito cada una, supongo que ni el mundo entero tendría lugar para todos los libros que resultarían.
es.R: Jesús también hizo muchas otras cosas. Si alguien las escribiera todas, una por una, ¡creo que en el mundo entero no habría lugar para tantos libros!

fr.L: Et il y a aussi beaucoup d’autres choses que Jésus fit ; si on les écrivait une à une, le monde lui-même, je suppose, ne pourrait pas contenir les livres qu’on écrirait.
fr.B: Jésus fit encore bien d’autres choses. Si on les écrivait une par une, je suppose que le monde lui-même ne pourrait pas contenir tous les livres qu’il faudrait écrire.
fr.R: Jésus a fait aussi beaucoup d’autres choses. Si on les écrivait toutes, une par une, je ne pense pas que le monde entier aurait assez de place pour tous les livres qu’il faudrait écrire !

sw.L: Na yapo pia mambo mengine mengi aliyoyatenda Yesu; kama yangeandikwa kila moja kwa kipekee, nadhani vitabu vinavyoandikwa visingeenea hata katika ulimwengu wenyewe.
sw.B: Yesu alifanya pia mambo mengine mengi. Kama kila moja lingeandikwa, nadhani ulimwengu wote usingekuwa na nafasi ya kutosha kwa vitabu vyote ambavyo vingeandikwa.
sw.R: Yesu alifanya pia mambo mengine mengi sana. Kama yote yangeandikwa moja baada ya jingine, sidhani kwamba ulimwengu mzima ungekuwa na nafasi ya vitabu vyote ambavyo vingeandikwa!

vi.L: Và cũng có nhiều việc khác mà Đức Giê-xu đã làm; nếu từng việc được chép ra, tôi nghĩ chính thế gian cũng không chứa nổi những sách được viết ra.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu còn làm nhiều việc khác nữa. Nếu từng việc một đều được ghi chép lại, tôi nghĩ cả thế gian này cũng không chứa hết số sách sẽ được viết ra.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu còn làm nhiều việc khác nữa. Nếu ghi lại hết từng việc một, tôi nghĩ cả thế gian cũng không có đủ chỗ để chứa hết những cuốn sách ấy!

ko.L: 그런데 예수께서 행하신 다른 일들도 많이 있는데, 그것들을 하나하나 기록한다면, 기록될 책들을 세상 자체도 담지 못할 것이라고 나는 생각한다.
ko.B: 예수께서 하신 일은 이 밖에도 많이 있다. 그것을 낱낱이 기록한다면, 세상이라도 그 기록된 책들을 다 담아 두지 못할 것이라고 나는 생각한다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 이 밖에도 많은 일을 하셨다. 그 일들을 하나하나 다 적는다면, 그렇게 적은 책들을 온 세상에 다 둘 곳이 없을 것이라고 나는 생각한다!

decisions.choice: the Gospel ends with "books" (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "Amen" at the end, as copyists often did at the close of a book; the earliest do not have it. It has been held that the first scribe of Codex Sinaiticus ended the Gospel at verse 24 and that verse 25 was added afterward, but photographs of the page taken under ultraviolet light show verse 25 written by the first scribe. Some manuscripts of one family place the story of the woman caught in adultery (7:53-8:11) after this verse. A footnote gives "Amen". A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: not even the world could hold the books: an overstatement for effect
decisions.reason: The writer does not mean a calculation. He says in a vivid way what 20:30 says plainly: what has been written is a small part of what Jesus did, and his works are beyond counting. "The world" here is the whole earth. Writers of the time used the same kind of figure to praise a subject too great to tell in full.

decisions.choice: I suppose: the only place in John where the narrator says "I"
decisions.reason: After the "we" of verse 24, a single writer speaks in the first person for the only time in the Gospel. It may be the disciple himself, or the one who finished the book; John does not say. The word is modest: it gives the writer's own judgment.

decisions.choice: many other things that Jesus did: all his deeds, not only the signs
decisions.reason: The sentence echoes 20:30 ("many other signs ... not written in this book") but widens it to everything Jesus did. With it the Gospel closes, as it opened (1:1-3), on the greatness of the one it is about.

decisions.choice: I suppose (L, B); I do not think (R); contain (L); hold (B); have room for (R); one by one (L); each one (B); every one of them (R)
decisions.reason: "Suppose" keeps the writer's modest tone (meaning decision m3); Readable says the same in everyday words, with an exclamation mark to show that the words are an overstatement (m2). Balanced puts "Jesus did many other things" first, as natural word order; Readable keeps the word "world", as every level does.

decisions.choice: supongo (L, B); creo (R); podría contener (L); tendría lugar para (B); no habría lugar para (R); una a una (L); cada una (B); una por una (R)
decisions.reason: "Supongo" keeps the writer's modest tone (meaning decision m3); Readable says the same in everyday words, with exclamation marks to show that the words are an overstatement (m2). Balanced puts "Jesús hizo" first, as natural word order; every level keeps "el mundo".

decisions.choice: nadhani vitabu vinavyoandikwa visingeenea hata katika ulimwengu wenyewe (L)
alternatives: nadhani hata ulimwengu wenyewe usingeweza kuvipokea vitabu vinavyoandikwa
decisions.reason: In Swahili the books are the natural subject of "kuenea" (to fit, to have room), so Literal makes them the subject and keeps every word of the Greek. "Nadhani" (I suppose) keeps the writer's modest tone (meaning decision m3); Readable says "sidhani" (I do not think), and all three levels keep "ulimwengu" (the world).

decisions.choice: the narrator says "tôi"
decisions.reason: The only place the narrator says "I"; the plain first person "tôi" keeps it personal and modest.
